learn.title: From C to assembly
learn.body: The compiler reads the preprocessed text and checks it: is the grammar right, do the types fit? If so, it writes assembly, a readable list of instructions for your CPU. If not, it prints an error and stops.

learn.title: Stop at assembly
learn.body: The `-S` flag stops after compiling and saves the assembly in `prog.s`. It differs between CPU types, so it is not portable.

learn.title: A compile error
learn.body: The `;` after the `printf` call is missing. The compiler stops near line 4 and builds nothing.

learn.title: Reading the message
learn.body: A message looks like `prog.c:4:19: error: ...`: file, line, column, then the problem. Fix the first error first. Later ones are often just fallout from it. Wording differs between clang and gcc.

learn.title: The flags we use
learn.body: `-o prog` names the program, otherwise it is `a.out`. `-Wall -Wextra` switch on more warnings, and `-std=c11` picks the language version.

learn.title: One compile, step by step
learn.body: Follow `cc prog.c -o prog` with a typo in `prog.c`.
steps: The preprocessor expands headers and macros
The compiler checks grammar and types
It finds the typo, prints file and line, and stops
No program is made, so there is nothing to run

questions.prompt: Put the four stages in order.
questions.explanation: Text is expanded, turned into assembly, then machine code, then joined into one program.

questions.prompt: What does the compiler write when it succeeds?
questions.explanation: The assembler and linker come after the compiler. The compiler's own output is assembly.

questions.prompt: Which flag stops after compiling and saves assembly? Type it.
A missing semicolon is found by which stage?
An error appears at line 4 and at line 9. Which do you fix first?
questions.explanation: Later errors are often caused by the first one, so fix from the top.

questions.prompt: To name the finished program `prog`, add \_\_ prog.
questions.explanation: `-o` sets the output file name. Without it you get `a.out`.

questions.prompt: Match each flag to its job.
questions.explanation: These flags control where the build stops and how talkative it is.
